acceptance_criteria.text: Migration 0012 is idempotent and safe to re-run on every ingest (init_db re-applies all migrations): `create table if not exists`, `create or replace view` only for NEW views, `drop policy if exists` before `create policy`, no unguarded INSERT/seed, no ALTER/DROP/REPLACE of any existing table or view (transactions_normalized, transactions_categorized, spend_by_category, monthly_movement, balance_reconciliation, transactions_flow, monthly_flows, existing tables).

acceptance_criteria.text: Every new table has RLS enabled plus a `deny_all` policy (for all to public using (false) with check (false)) following the 0011 pattern, inside 0012; every new view is created with `security_invoker = on`. 0011's hard-coded target list is not edited.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest static test parses 0012: for each `create table` there is `enable row level security` + `drop policy if exists deny_all` + `create policy deny_all ... using (false) with check (false)`; each `create ... view` carries `with (security_invoker = on)` or a matching `alter view ... set (security_invoker = on)`.

acceptance_criteria.text: Matcher is a pure, deterministic function (transactions x beneficiary snapshot -> matches): output independent of input ordering, dict/set iteration, DB row order, clock and locale. Normalisation (casefold, whitespace collapse, documented punctuation handling) is pure and unit-tested. Rule precedence is a fixed ordered list, highest confidence first.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: same inputs under several permutations of transactions and beneficiaries -> identical match output; normalisation unit tests; no datetime.now/random usage inside the matcher module (grep).

acceptance_criteria.text: DEBIT-only: only rows with upper(type)='DEBIT' / amount < 0 are candidates; CREDIT rows never match, regardless of description.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: CREDIT row whose description exactly equals a beneficiary name/reference -> no match; equivalent DEBIT row -> match.

acceptance_criteria.text: Payment-type gate: only rows whose transaction_type is in an explicit, code-defined allowlist are candidates; NULL/unknown types fail closed; card purchases, fees, ATM and debit orders never match. CONDITIONAL on Q2 for the allowlist contents.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest parametrized: each allowlisted type matches; CardPurchases, FeesAndInterest, ATMWithdrawals, DebitOrders, None, and an unknown string -> no match; allowlist is a single module-level constant.

acceptance_criteria.text: Fail-closed: 0 candidates -> no match; >1 distinct beneficiaryIds under the highest-precedence rule that fired -> no match (status 'ambiguous' if stored), with no fall-through to a weaker rule to break ties. Minimum token-length guards apply; no fuzzy/edit-distance matching (no difflib/Levenshtein).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest golden fixtures: 'Acme' vs 'Acme Trading', 'J Smith' vs 'J Smithers', two beneficiaries with same name, short tokens ('Mom','Rent') below guard -> no match; single clean candidate -> match; grep matcher for difflib/SequenceMatcher -> none.

acceptance_criteria.text: Explainable: every stored match records match_rule (e.g. reference_exact, name_exact, reference_prefix) and matched_token (the normalised beneficiary-side token that hit, never a full account number), plus beneficiary_id and the snapshot identifier/matched_at.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: each positive fixture yields non-empty match_rule from the documented rule set and matched_token equal to the expected normalised token; 0012 table has match_rule and matched_token NOT NULL columns.

acceptance_criteria.text: Idempotent: re-running sync+match with the same transactions and snapshot produces an identical match set with no duplicate rows and no flip-flop (upsert keyed on transaction_hash or full deterministic recompute).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: run match persistence twice against fake DB -> identical SQL params / identical resulting rows; unique key on transaction_hash in 0012 (or equivalent).

acceptance_criteria.text: Own-account transfers excluded: rows with transactions_flow.flow_type='internal_transfer' are never matched, and any beneficiary whose digit-normalised accountNumber equals an own accounts.account_number is never a candidate (own account at another bank remains eligible).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: beneficiary with own Investec account number + matching DEBIT description -> no match; internal_transfer-flagged row -> no match; view SQL filters flow_type <> 'internal_transfer'.

open_questions.q: Beneficiary account number: persist and display the FULL number, or last-3 only (masked ****709)? The user explicitly wants to see the account number; domain/repo convention (payments tables, L-0003, POPIA minimisation) is last-3.
open_questions.recommended_default: Honour the user's request: persist the full accountNumber in the new beneficiary table only (behind deny_all RLS + security_invoker view, included in encrypted backups only if BACKUP_PASSPHRASE set), display it in full in the view, never log/print it and never put it in matched_token; do NOT store cellNo/emailAddress/raw. If the human prefers stricter POPIA posture: last-3 only + in-memory own-account check persisted as is_own_account boolean.
open_questions.resolution: APPROVED by human: store + show FULL beneficiary account number (new table only, deny_all RLS, never logged, not in matched_token; no cellNo/email/raw).

open_questions.q: Which transactionType values count as payments/transfers (vocabulary is unverified in repo)?
open_questions.recommended_default: Human runs `select transaction_type, count(*) from transactions where type='DEBIT' group by 1` on prod and the result is frozen as a code constant. Provisional allowlist until confirmed: OnlineBankingPayments, OnlineBankingTransfers, FasterPay; explicitly excluded: CardPurchases, FeesAndInterest, ATMWithdrawals, DebitOrders; NULL/unknown fail closed.
open_questions.resolution: Human approved defaults without supplying prod query: provisional allowlist OnlineBankingPayments, OnlineBankingTransfers, FasterPay as a code constant; NULL/unknown fail closed. Revisit when human runs the type-count query.

open_questions.q: Trigger sync+match as a gated hook inside `ingest`, or via a new subcommand?
open_questions.recommended_default: Gated ingest hook (flag off by default), mirroring the non-fatal balance-fetch pattern; no new subcommand, so CLI help stays byte-identical. A new subcommand would require additive-only help change + re-baseline.
open_questions.resolution: Default approved: gated hook inside ingest, no new subcommand; CLI help byte-identical.

open_questions.q: Snapshot semantics: freeze past matches at match time, or recompute all against the latest beneficiary snapshot?
open_questions.recommended_default: Freeze: existing 'matched' rows keep their beneficiary_id/rule/token/snapshot id; only unmatched/ambiguous rows (and new rows) are re-evaluated against the latest snapshot. Beneficiaries are soft-retired, never hard-deleted.
open_questions.resolution: Default approved: freeze existing matches; re-evaluate only unmatched/ambiguous/new rows; soft-retire beneficiaries.

open_questions.q: Name-field precedence: does referenceName (my-reference) rank above beneficiaryName, and where does `name` sit?
open_questions.recommended_default: account-number digit signal (>=8 digits) > referenceName exact > beneficiaryName exact > name exact > guarded prefix (min length guard, e.g. >6 chars); confirm referenceName semantics against one real payload before freeze.
open_questions.resolution: Default approved: account-digit signal (>=8 digits) > referenceName exact > beneficiaryName exact > name exact > guarded prefix (>6 chars).

open_questions.q: Surface a 'Paid to' column in the weekly report and/or statement Excel?
open_questions.recommended_default: No for this run: keep both workbooks unchanged (F10 strict); the DB view is the read surface. Revisit in a later run if wanted.
open_questions.resolution: Default approved: no Excel change this run; F10 strict.
